structured_output.summary: Pulsator with -1523 ppm P/2 modulation and inconsistent sector depths; Sectors 112-114 can test.
reasons: Disagree with the mechanical 'proposed for submission': the target itself is a known pulsator (vsx_variables: Gaia DR3 6064573197263477376 DSCT|GDOR|SXPHE at 0"), and step 9 finds a coherent modulation at half the candidate period of ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -1523 +/- 118 ppm (13 sigma, same sign in all six sectors, ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm_by_sector -1179 to -1823). The amplitude is 1.8 times the fit_depth_ppm of 863 and the negative sign is unphysical for ellipsoidal variation, so this is more likely a gamma Dor mode near 2.7 c/d locked to the search period, which makes a pulsation-driven false alarm a real possibility. The pipeline raised no caution for it.

Sector depths from the QLP light curves are inconsistent: sector_depth_consistency_p_value 7.08e-14, with depth_ppm_by_sector running from S102 1874 +/- 167 to S101 123 +/- 147 (consistent with zero). The cutout depths are more consistent (cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.278) but S102 r2.0 gives 995 +/- 217 against 1874 in QLP, so the depth that triggered the search looks inflated by detrending of the stellar variability. The all-sector figure shows a dip in S102, S11, S38, S99 and S100, weak in S65 and absent in S101.

The other-sector evidence is weaker than expected everywhere: other_sector_results gives S65 SNR 8.8 vs expected 12.9, S99 9.4 vs 13.0, S100 10.5 vs 14.8, S101 12.4 vs 14.4; joint_search_snr 8.4 (joint_search_detected True, joint_search_highest_null_snr 5.0) is below the single-sector S102 BLS SNR of 12.3 recorded in the verification record, which fits a signal whose apparent depth varies between sectors.

Localisation supports the target but rests mainly on one sector: pixel_verdicts_by_sector gives S102 on target (SNR 7.3) and S100 unresolved (SNR 5.5), while S11, S38, S65, S99 and S101 are too faint and the best star wanders among unrelated neighbours; joint_pixel_verdict is on target with joint_difference_image_snr 9.7. The field is crowded (gaia_neighbours 176, 33 listed in gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip, the closest Gaia DR3 6064573197263478784 at 12" G 17.6 needing 40%), which is the pipeline's only caution.

Evidence in favour that keeps this from a drop: triceratops_verdict likely planet with fpp_mean 0.0377 +/- 0.0012 and nfpp_mean 0 (nearby_scenarios_excluded True); odd_even_difference_sigma 0.75; secondary_depth_ppm 160 +/- 68 below secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 289; gaia_rv_variable False with gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0494 from 21 transits; gaia_ruwe 0.93; stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.24.

The candidate is not a star by size: planet_radius_earth_radii 5.83 +/- 0.32 with transit_grazing False and fit_impact_parameter 0.388 +/- 0.2695, so the radius is constrained and well below 22.4 Earth radii. A 5.8 Earth-radius body at period_days 0.735 and fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 2.38 around a stellar_radius_solar_radii 1.85 star with gaia_vbroad_km_s 64 would be a rare ultra-short-period sub-Saturn, plausible but unusual enough to want the variability question settled first.
No catalogue conflict: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, and ephemeris_match_likely_sources is empty, so the signal would be new if it is real.

What would decide it: unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 112 113 114 will add three sectors of 200 s cadence for the sector depth consistency test and the per-sector pixel check; if the dip recurs at the fit ephemeris (fit_period_days 0.7349930 +/- 0.00000109) with depth near 863 ppm in all three it supports a transit, while depths swinging again between ~0 and ~1900 ppm support pulsation beating. A periodogram of the existing light curve showing whether a pulsation mode sits at 1/P or 2/P (about 1.36 or 2.72 c/d) would decide it sooner.
